hindi: बारह वर्ष की स्त्री व्यवहार को प्राप्त होती है, सोलह वर्ष का पुरुष व्यवहार को प्राप्त होता है।
english: A woman of twelve years becomes one who has reached dealings (vyavahāra); a man [is so] at sixteen years.
notes: The second clause has no predicate; bhavati is carried over (bracketed in English, supplied without bracket in Hindi). vyavahāra is kept literal as "dealings"; the sense (legal capacity / majority) is not stated in the line and is not imported.

hindi: इसके बाद आज्ञा का पालन न करने पर स्त्री का दण्ड बारह पण है, पुरुष का दुगुना। — यह शुश्रूषा है।
english: After this, in disobedience, the penalty on a woman is twelve paṇas, on a man double. — Such is obedience (śuśrūṣā).
notes: ata ūrdhvam = "after this / from this onward"; what "this" refers to (the age of 12/16 of unit 1) is not stated. a-śuśrūṣā = non-obedience; śuśrūṣā (literally "wish to hear, attendance") rendered "obedience", alternative "service". striyā is instrumental ("by the woman"), a regular usage of this text for the person on whom the penalty falls. The closing "iti śuśrūṣā" is a section label ("Such is śuśrūṣā").

words.gloss: in the woman to be maintained

hindi: जिस भरण योग्य स्त्री के लिए समय निर्दिष्ट न हो, उसके विषय में ग्रास-आच्छादन अथवा उससे अधिक, पुरुष के परिवाप के अनुसार, कुछ अधिक सहित दे।
english: In the case of a woman to be maintained, for whom no time is specified, [one] should give food and clothing, or more, with something extra, according to the person's parivāpa.
notes: bharmaṇyā: derived from bharman/bharma "maintenance" (cf. the closing label "iti bharma" of unit 6), taken as "fit to be maintained"; rendered literally. parivāpa is obscure and kept untranslated (doubt; commentators differ on "means / expenditure / outlay"). puruṣa can be "man" or "person"; "person" kept as the neutral sense. The subject of dadyāt is not stated ("[one]"). saviśeṣam read as "with something extra" (literally "with a distinction/surplus"); vā-adhikam = "or more".

hindi: जिसके लिए समय निर्दिष्ट हो, उसके विषय में उसी को गिनकर तथा बन्ध दे।
english: In the case of [a woman] for whom the time is specified, having reckoned that very [thing], [one] should also give a bond (bandha).
notes: "tad eva" = "that very [thing]"; the text does not say what is reckoned (presumably the food and clothing of unit 3); not supplied. bandha = bond, binding (alternatives: security, pledge, restraint); rendered "bond", medium confidence. Feminine locative nirdiṣṭa-kālāyām implies the woman of unit 3. The subject of dadyāt is not stated.

hindi: तथा शुल्क, स्त्रीधन और आधिवेदनिक के न लिए जाने पर।
english: And in the non-taking of the śulka, the strī-dhana (woman's property) and the ādhivedanika.
notes: Fragment continuing into unit 6 (the husband is not to be proceeded against); the main clause is in unit 6. a-ādāna = "non-taking" (non-receiving); who does not take is not stated. The sense could also be "non-payment". śulka is kept as a term (bride-price, or toll/duty elsewhere in the text). ādhivedanika is obscure and kept untranslated (it is formed on ādhivedana); strī-dhana is rendered literally. Compound taken as a three-member dvandva.

words.gloss: one who has entered the father-in-law's family

hindi: ससुर के कुल में प्रविष्ट होने पर अथवा अलग हो जाने पर पति पर अभियोग नहीं चलाना चाहिए। — यह भरण है।
english: When [she] has entered the father-in-law's family, or is separated, the husband is not to be proceeded against. — Such is maintenance (bharma).
notes: Continues unit 5 (non-taking of śulka, strī-dhana, ādhivedanika). The woman is not named (feminine locatives); "[she]" supplied in English only. vibhaktā = separated/divided (the nature of the separation is not stated). abhiyojya = to be charged/proceeded against. Closing "iti bharma" is a section label ("Such is bharma"); Hindi uses the usual word भरण for bharma.

hindi: “हे नष्ट हुई”, “हे विनष्ट हुई”, “हे विकलाङ्गी”, “हे पितृहीना”, “हे मातृहीना” — बिना निर्देश किए विनय ग्रहण कराना है।
english: “O lost one”, “O ruined one”, “O maimed one”, “O fatherless one”, “O motherless one” — without specifying [the fault], [there is] the making [her] take discipline.
notes: Low confidence. The five quoted words are read as feminine vocatives (a form of address), because they end in -e and are quoted; the alternative is a locative reading ("in [a case of] the lost, the ruined, the maimed, the fatherless, the motherless"). nyaṅga is obscure (ny-aṅga: "maimed / low-limbed"); rendered "maimed" with doubt. The closing iti is carried by the quotation marks. anirdeśa = non-specification; vinaya-grāhaṇa = causing to take/receive discipline (caus. noun); who gives the discipline and to whom is not stated (the "[her]" is a supply). The predicate is a bare copula.

hindi: अथवा बाँस की खपच्ची, रस्सी, हाथ में से किसी एक से पीठ पर तीन बार प्रहार।
english: Or a striking on the back three times with any one of a split bamboo, a rope, [or] a hand.
notes: dala = piece / split / leaf; veṇu-dala "split of bamboo" (bamboo splinter). Compound taken as a three-member dvandva (veṇu-dala, rajju, hasta), as the genitive plural with anyatama requires. No predicate; bare copula understood.

words.gloss: by the two penalties for verbal and physical injury

hindi: उसका उल्लंघन होने पर वाक्-पारुष्य और दण्ड-पारुष्य, इन दोनों के दण्डों से आधे दण्ड होते हैं।
english: In the transgression of that, [there are] half-penalties, by the two penalties for verbal injury (vāk-pāruṣya) and physical injury (daṇḍa-pāruṣya).
notes: "tasya" (of that) is not clear: the beating of unit 8 or the discipline of unit 7; who transgresses is not stated. vāg-daṇḍa-pāruṣya-daṇḍābhyām is read as an abbreviated dvandva "vāk-pāruṣya and daṇḍa-pāruṣya" plus daṇḍābhyām (dual: the two penalties), i.e. half of each of the two penalties. Alternative: half-penalties "for harshness of speech and harshness of punishment". Rendered per the fixed Book 3 terms.

words.gloss: of one whose fault is notorious

hindi: वही दण्ड स्त्री के लिए, पति के विषय में, उसका है जिसका दोष प्रसिद्ध है।
english: That very [penalty applies] to a woman, towards [her] husband, [in the case] of one whose fault is notorious.
notes: Low confidence: the cases do not agree (striyā instrumental, prasiddha-doṣāyāḥ genitive); the sense appears to be that the same (half) penalty falls on a woman, in respect of her husband, when her fault is notorious. Whose fault (the woman's or the husband's) is not certain from the grammar (doṣāyāḥ is feminine). "tad eva" = the same penalty as in unit 9 (not stated). Not flagged as a typo because striyā is used instrumentally elsewhere in this chunk; a reviewer may consider striyāḥ.

hindi: ईर्ष्या से बाहरी विहारों में तथा द्वारों पर अत्यय जैसा निर्दिष्ट है वैसा है। — यह पारुष्य है।
english: Out of jealousy, in outside amusements [and] at the doors, the penalty is as specified. — Such is harshness (pāruṣya).
notes: Who acts out of jealousy, and what is done in the amusements and at the doors (confining, abusing), is not stated; the line is rendered literally. Possibly "in outside amusements" and "at the doors" are two separate occasions; no "and" is printed. atyaya = penalty (as in the fixed rendering). Closing "iti pāruṣyam" is a section label.

words.gram: pres. part. ātm. f. nom. sg. a-√maṇḍ (caus.)

hindi: पति से द्वेष करने वाली स्त्री, सात ऋतुकालों तक शृंगार न करती हुई, उसी समय रखने योग्य आभूषण रखकर, दूसरी स्त्री के साथ सोए हुए पति के विरुद्ध कार्यवाही करे।
english: A woman hating [her] husband, not adorning [herself] for seven menstrual periods, at that very time, having laid down the ornaments to be deposited, should proceed against the husband who is lying with another [woman].
notes: Low confidence on the verb: anu-√śī (anuśayīta) literally "lie along / follow up"; the sense "lodge a complaint / sue / proceed against" is taken from the context (the husband is the object) and is not certain; alternatives: "complain to the authorities", "bear a grudge". ārtava = relating to the ṛtu; "menstrual period" taken, medium confidence. sthāpya-ābharaṇa "ornaments to be deposited/kept" is obscure (what is deposited, with whom, is not stated). amaṇḍayamānā takes an unstated "herself". The first bhartāram is the object of dviṣatī; the second is the object of anuśayīta.

words.gloss: of female mendicant, anvādhi, kin, family

hindi: अथवा द्वेष करने वाला पति भिक्षुकी, अन्वाधि, ज्ञाति और कुल में से किसी एक में एक स्त्री के विरुद्ध कार्यवाही करे।
english: Or the husband, hating [her], in any one of the female mendicant, the anvādhi, the kin [and] the family, should proceed against a single woman.
notes: Low confidence. anvādhi is obscure and kept untranslated. The compound is taken as a four-member dvandva (bhikṣukī, anvādhi, jñāti, kula); alternatively jñāti-kula "family of kinsmen" is one member. What the locative anyatame refers to (persons, places, cases) is not stated. ekām = "one / a single" (alternative: "only one"). anuśayīta as in unit 12 (doubtful sense).

words.gloss: in approaching a spy of the same varṇa

hindi: चिह्न देखे जाने पर, मैथुन के अपहरण में, अथवा समान वर्ण के गुप्तचर के पास पहुँचने में झूठ बोलने वाला बारह पण दे।
english: When a sign is seen, in the carrying off [concerning] sexual union, or in approaching a spy of the same varṇa, one speaking falsely should pay twelve paṇas.
notes: Low confidence; all three locatives are obscure. dṛṣṭa-liṅga "when a sign has been seen" (a mark/sign of what is not stated). maithuna-apahāra: "carrying off / removal [concerning] sexual union" (alternatives: abduction, concealment, taking away for sexual purposes). savarṇa: "of the same varṇa/colour" (or "with the same appearance"); apasarpa = spy as in the fixed glossary; upagama = approach. Who is the false speaker (accuser, witness) is not stated; mithyā-vādin "one speaking falsely".

hindi: पति के न चाहने पर द्वेष करने वाली पत्नी छोड़ने योग्य नहीं है; तथा पत्नी के न चाहने पर पति।
english: A wife who hates [him] is not to be released when the husband does not desire [it]; and [likewise] the husband [who hates], when the wife [does not desire it].
notes: Read as a genitive absolute: bhartur akāmasya "of the husband not desiring [release]" with amokṣyā dviṣatī bhāryā; the second half is elliptical ("and the husband of the wife", i.e. the hating husband when the wife is unwilling). Alternative reading: "a wife hating a husband who does not desire [it]". The object of dviṣatī is not printed. Hindi leaves the elliptical second half as printed.

hindi: परस्पर द्वेष से मोक्ष होता है।
english: Release [comes] from mutual hatred.

text_flags.why: possible: anusvāra on the first member of a compound marked with a dot; the compound member should be the bare stem paraspara (alternatively an adverb parasparam followed by dveṣāt, but then no dot).

notes: Copula understood ("comes").

hindi: अथवा स्त्री के दुर्व्यवहार के कारण यदि पुरुष मोक्ष चाहे तो जैसा लिया गया हो वैसा इसे दे।
english: Or if the man desires release because of the woman's ill-treatment, [he] should give to her [it] as it was taken.
notes: yathā-gṛhītam "as taken" has no stated object (presumably what was received at the marriage, not imported); the object is bracketed in English. viprakāra = ill-treatment.

hindi: अथवा पुरुष के दुर्व्यवहार के कारण यदि स्त्री मोक्ष चाहे तो जैसा लिया गया हो वैसा इसे न दे।
english: Or if the woman desires release because of the man's ill-treatment, [one] should not give to her [it] as it was taken.
notes: Low confidence on who gives and what: the subject of dadyāt is not stated (in unit 17 the man; here "[one]"), and the dative asyai ("to her") rules out the woman herself as giver. The result (the woman gets nothing back although the man ill-treated her) looks odd; a reviewer may check the edition (possible variant or corrupt reading). Rendered literally.

hindi: धर्म-विवाहों का मोक्ष नहीं होता। — यह द्वेष है।
english: There is no release of dharma marriages. — Such is hatred (dveṣa).
notes: dharma-vivāha = marriage of the dharma type (the text's technical term for the approved forms of marriage; no list is imported). Closing "iti dveṣaḥ" is a section label.

hindi: दर्प, मद्य और क्रीड़ा के विषय में निषेध की गई स्त्री तीन पण का दण्ड दे।
english: A woman who has been forbidden, in pride, liquor [and] play, should pay a penalty of three paṇas.
notes: The compound darpa-madya-krīḍā is taken as a dvandva (pride, liquor, play); alternatively "play of pride and liquor" or "arrogant sport with liquor". krīḍā = play, sport (possibly gambling or pleasure-making). Who forbids her is not stated.

words.gloss: in going to women's spectacles and amusements
in going to men's spectacles and amusements

hindi: दिन में स्त्रियों के प्रेक्षा-विहार में जाने पर छह पण का दण्ड है; पुरुषों के प्रेक्षा-विहार में जाने पर बारह पण।
english: By day, in going to women's spectacles [and] amusements the penalty is six paṇas; in going to men's spectacles [and] amusements, twelve paṇas.
notes: strī-prekṣā-vihāra can also be read "going to amuse oneself by looking at women" (prekṣā = looking, spectacle); rendered as spectacle-amusement of women/men. The second penalty (dvādaśa-paṇaḥ) omits daṇḍaḥ. The person on whom the penalty falls is not stated (the woman, as in the surrounding units).

hindi: रात में दुगुना।
english: At night, double.
notes: Refers to the penalty of unit 21; not repeated.

words.gloss: in the going out of one asleep or drunk

hindi: सोए हुए, मत्त के बाहर निकलने पर तथा पति के लिए द्वार न देने पर बारह पण।
english: In the going out of [one who is] asleep [or] drunk, and in the non-giving of the door to the husband: twelve paṇas.
notes: supta-matta-pravrajana: the person who is asleep or drunk (the woman, or the husband whom she leaves) is not stated; the compound is rendered literally as "going out of one asleep or drunk". pravrajana = going forth / going out. bhartur adāne dvārasya: both bhartuḥ and dvārasya are genitives; read "non-giving of the door to the husband"; alternative "the husband's non-giving of the door". "[or]" is supplied for the unmarked pair supta/matta. Penalty daṇḍa omitted.

hindi: रात में निकलने पर दुगुना।
english: In going out at night, double.
notes: niṣkasana = going out (from ni-ṣ-kas; alternatively "expulsion / leaving the house"); who goes out is not stated. Double of the penalty of unit 23 (twelve paṇas).

words.gloss: for the purpose of sexual union

hindi: स्त्री और पुरुष के, मैथुन के प्रयोजन से अङ्गों की चेष्टा में अथवा एकान्त में अश्लील बातचीत में, स्त्री का दण्ड चौबीस पण है; पुरुष का दुगुना।
english: Of woman and man, in movements of the limbs for the purpose of sexual union, or in indecent talk in secret: the penalty on the woman is twenty-four paṇas; on the man, double.
notes: viceṣṭā = movement, gesture. arthena is the instrumental of artha used as "for the purpose of". raho is read with aślīla-sambhāṣā ("in secret, indecent talk"); it may also govern both phrases. striyā is instrumental (see unit 2).

words.gloss: in taking hold of hair, nīvi, teeth, nails

hindi: केश, नीवी, दाँत और नख को पकड़ने में प्रथम साहस-दण्ड है; पुरुष का दुगुना।
english: In taking hold of the hair, the nīvi, the teeth [or] the nails, the first fine for rashness; on the man, double.
notes: nīvi = the waist-knot / tie of the lower garment (medium confidence), kept as nīvi. ālambana = taking hold of / grasping. "pūrva" = first (of the three grades of sāhasa-daṇḍa, grades not stated here). No predicate; bare copula understood.

hindi: शंकित स्थान में तथा बातचीत में पण के स्थान पर शिफा-दण्ड है।
english: In a suspected place and in conversation: in place of a paṇa, the śiphā penalty.
notes: śiphā is obscure and kept untranslated (literally a lash / strap / root-fibre; "lash" is the probable sense, low confidence). paṇa-sthāne = "in place of a paṇa" (alternatively "where the penalty stands at a paṇa"). śaṅkita-sthāna = "suspected place" or "place of suspicion". Whether "in a suspected place" and "in conversation" are two cases or one is not clear ("sambhāṣāyāṃ ca").

words.gloss: in the middle of the village
at an interval of a pakṣa

hindi: स्त्रियों को गाँव के बीच में चाण्डाल पक्ष के अन्तर पर पाँच शिफा दे।
english: The caṇḍāla should give women five śiphās in the middle of the village, at an interval of a pakṣa.

text_flags.why: possible: an object of dadyāt should be accusative plural (śiphāḥ) or a collective dvigu in -m; the printed -ā is a nominative singular.

notes: Low confidence. strīṇām is a genitive ("of women"), rendered "to women" as the sense requires. pakṣa-antare: pakṣa has many senses (fortnight, side, wing, party); "at an interval of a pakṣa" is literal; alternatives: "after a fortnight", "on the other side (of the body)", "in the other camp". śiphā as in unit 27 (kept, probably a lash). caṇḍāla is a class name, kept.

hindi: अथवा पण वाले प्रहार को छुड़वाए। — यह अतीचार है।
english: Or [one] should cause a blow of a paṇa to be released. — Such is transgression (atīcāra).
notes: Low confidence. paṇika = "of a paṇa / at a paṇa"; the likely sense is that each blow may be released (commuted) for a paṇa, but the line says only "release a blow of a paṇa"; nothing is imported. The subject of mokṣayet is not stated. Closing "ity atīcāraḥ" is a section label.

hindi: निषिद्ध किए गए स्त्री और पुरुष के परस्पर उपकार में, छोटे द्रव्यों का दण्ड बारह पण है, मोटे द्रव्यों का चौबीस पण, धन और सोने का चौवन पण; यह स्त्री का दण्ड है, पुरुष का दुगुना।
english: Of the forbidden woman and man, in mutual favour: the penalty is twelve paṇas for small things, twenty-four paṇas for coarse things, fifty-four paṇas for money and gold — the penalty on the woman; on the man, double.

text_flags.why: possible: puṃsoḥ is a genitive dual ("of two men"); the parallel clauses in units 2, 25, 26 read puṃso dvi.guṇaḥ (genitive singular).

notes: upakāra = favour, help (here probably the giving of things; not stated). kṣudraka = small, sthūlaka = coarse (alternative: large); hiraṇya rendered "money", suvarṇa "gold". catuṣ-pañcāśat = fifty-four. The unit of the penalty for the second and third classes is paṇa as printed. striyā is instrumental (see unit 2).

words.gloss: of the two not to be approached
in dealings with a forbidden man

hindi: वे ही दण्ड, जो पहुँचने के अयोग्य हैं उन दोनों के लिए, आधे दण्ड हैं, तथा निषिद्ध पुरुष के साथ व्यवहारों में। — यह प्रतिषेध है।
english: Those very [penalties] are half-penalties for the two who are not to be approached, and likewise in dealings with a forbidden man. — Such is prohibition (pratiṣedha).
notes: agamya = "not to be approached / not to be gone to"; who the two are (and the nature of the prohibition) is not stated. Compound pratiṣiddha-puruṣa-vyavahāra is taken as "dealings with a forbidden man"; alternatively "dealings of a forbidden man". Closing "iti pratiṣedhaḥ" is a section label.

words.gloss: by what the king hates and by transgression
of woman's property and brought śulka

hindi: राजा द्वारा द्वेष किए गए कार्य से तथा अतिचार से, और स्वयं चले जाने से, स्त्रीधन और लाए गए शुल्क पर स्त्री का स्वामित्व नहीं रहता।
english: By [acts] hated by the king and by transgression, and by [her] own going away, non-ownership of the strī-dhana and of the śulka that has been brought arises for the woman.
notes: A verse (anuṣṭubh, 16 + 16 syllables). rāja-dviṣṭa-aticārābhyām (dual) = two items: what is hated by the king (rāja-dviṣṭa) and transgression (aticāra); rāja-dviṣṭa could also be a person hated by the king. ātma-apakramaṇa = going away of one's own accord (the woman's). strī-dhana-ānīta-śulka may be a three-member dvandva (woman's property, brought, śulka) or "strī-dhana and the śulka brought"; ānīta = brought (by whom/to whom is not stated). asvāmya = non-ownership (loss of ownership).
